newsitem.title: LATVIA: OLAINFARM BOURSE PRICE SEEN AT 1.5/1.9 LATS.
newsitem.headline: OLAINFARM BOURSE PRICE SEEN AT 1.5/1.9 LATS.

text.p: Olainfarm, a leading pharmaceutical company which starts bourse trading next week, is expected to show an initial price of 1.50 to 1.90 lats, below the price 2.50 lats where it traded as an OTC stock, dealers said on Friday.
The market capitalisation of one of Latvia's largest drugs makers along with Grindex could vary between 4.48 million lats and 5.68 million lats based on the these prices, dealers said.
The central depository registered 2.99 million shares and 51 percent or 1.53 million are held by strategic investor Olmafarm.
Some 1.32 million shares or 44 percent of Olainfarm stock were sold for vouchers.
Dealers said that a sale by Hansa Investments of a block of 909,091 shares earlier this year may affect the price when it starts quotation on the market.
"Hansa sold a bigger chunk of shares for 2.50 lats a piece, promising better first quarter results," Robert Idelsons, head of securities department with Trasta Bank said.
"It might be interested in trying to keep Olainfarm bourse price closer to 2.50 lats in order not to lose face on the result forecast they gave earlier," he added.
"I cannot think of a foreign investor today ready to pay more than two lats a share, given the reported first quarter losses and big debts," another dealer said.
Olainfarm registered a first quarter loss of 1.62 million lats on turnover of 1.79 million.
Olainfarm also has long-term debts of 2.2 million lats and short-term debts of 5.69 milion lats, the bourse said.
Olainfarm showed a free market price of some 2.50 lats per share against its face value of one lat during recent month.
The buying price has been lower, at 2.40-2.50 lats while the selling price has fluctuated between 2.40 to 2.65 lats.
Olainfarm specialises in organic synthesis products. Its main market is ready-made pharmaceuticals with 61 percent of sales in atvia and the CIS with 41 percent.
Substances for pharmaceutical production are mostly sold in western Europe.
Dealers said there has been considerable interest in Olainfarm shares, as intermediaries have been buying up shares to form bigger portfolios in the run-up to the bourse launch.
"It has mostly been a matter of buying locally and selling up north (in Estonia and Finland)," Andreta Petersone, a dealer with the Hansabank-Latvija said.
"There has been definitely more interest in Olainfarm among Estonian investors than locally," Trasta's Idelsons said.
"They expect a similar development scenario in Riga as on the Tallinn bourse and are attracted to banks and pharmaceutical companies, which are doing well there," he added.
Tallinn boasts an active pharmaceutical stock, Tallinna Farmatsiatehas. It has shown a steady growth in price during the last six months.
Vilnius bourse lists Sanitas, the country's biggest pahrmaceuticals producer, as an A group stock.
-- Martinsh Gravitis, Riga newsroom, +371 721 5240
